title: Phase 3: Category-Grouped Head-to-Head Report
description:
## Summary

New report format that groups bench results by category, showing per-category engine comparison table. This is the visible deliverable — proves WHERE contexting wins, not just THAT it wins.

## Report Format Mockup

```
=== Contexting vs find/grep ===

Category: concept-synonym (8 cases)

Tool          Hit@1   Hit@3   Hit@5   Avg Time   Avg Tokens
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
contexting    0.75    0.88    0.94    12ms       280
find          0.25    0.38    0.50    8ms        1,200
grep          0.50    0.63    0.75    45ms       3,400

Category: symbol-lookup (5 cases)

Tool          Hit@1   Hit@3   Hit@5   Avg Time   Avg Tokens
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
contexting    0.80    1.00    1.00    9ms        220
find          0.20    0.40    0.40    6ms        900
grep          0.60    0.80    0.80    38ms       2,100

═══ Overall (26 cases) ═══
Tool          Hit@1   Hit@3   Hit@5   Avg Time   Avg Tokens
contexting    0.77    0.92    0.96    11ms       255
find          0.23    0.39    0.47    7ms        1,080
grep          0.54    0.71    0.78    42ms       2,800
```

## Changes

### bench_report.go
- Add `printCategoryReport(results []EngineResult, cases []EvalCase)`:
  - Group results by `EvalCase.Category`
  - For each category: print header with case count, then per-engine summary row
  - After all categories: print overall summary
- Add `categoryReportToJSON(results []EngineResult, cases []EvalCase)`:
  - Structured JSON with per-category breakdown + overall
  - New struct `CategoryReport`:
    ```go
    type CategoryReport struct {
      Category  string                   `json:"category"`
      CaseCount int                      `json:"case_count"`
      Engines   []EngineSummary          `json:"engines"`
    }
    type FullReport struct {
      Categories []CategoryReport `json:"categories"`
      Overall    []EngineSummary   `json:"overall"`
    }
    ```
- Modify existing report functions to detect when cases have categories → use category report instead of flat report
- Keep flat report as fallback for v1 cases (no categories)

### command_bench.go
- When cases loaded via LoadCasesAuto have Category field set, use category-grouped report
- Add `--by-category` flag (default: true when v2 cases detected, false for v1)

## Tests (bench_test.go)
- TestCategoryReportGrouping — results grouped correctly by category
- TestCategoryReportJSON — JSON output has correct structure
- TestCategoryReportFallback — v1 cases (no category) use flat report
- TestOverallSummary — overall row aggregates across all categories correctly

## Dependencies
- Requires Phase 1 (contexting-hv4) — needs Category field on EvalCase
- Requires Phase 2 (contexting-7sl) — needs Hit@k and token fields on EngineResult/EngineSummary

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Category-grouped table report prints per-category engine comparison
- [ ] Overall summary aggregates across all categories
- [ ] JSON output includes structured per-category breakdown
- [ ] Falls back to flat report for v1 cases without categories
- [ ] --by-category flag controls report mode
- [ ] go test ./... passes
close_reason: Phase 3 complete. Category-grouped report with per-category tables + overall summary. --by-category flag. JSON output with FullReport struct. Falls back to flat for v1 cases.

title: Fix: Bootstrap snapshot staleness — watch misses changes made while not running
notes:
## Implementation Plan

### 1. Add ModTime field to Node struct
- File: node.go, Node struct (~line 13)
- Add ModTime int64 json:"mod_time,omitempty" after Symbols field
- Zero value means unknown — backward-compatible with existing context.json
- omitempty ensures excluded from JSON when 0

### 2. Update upsertNodeByRelPath to accept and set mtime
- File: node_mutation.go
- Add mtime int64 parameter
- Set node.ModTime = mtime when creating new node and updating existing
- Update isExistingDirectory to return mtime from info.ModTime().UnixNano()

### 3. Update ApplyChanges to pass mtime
- File: index_manager.go, ApplyChanges function
- Capture mtime from isExistingDirectory, pass through to upsertNodeByRelPath

### 4. Add collectFilesystemState helper
- File: index_manager.go (new function near Bootstrap)
- filepath.WalkDir with shouldIgnorePath (same as BuildTree)
- Returns map[string]fsEntry where fsEntry has mtime and isDir
- Only collect mtime for files (dirs get 0)

### 5. Add collectSnapshotPaths helper
- File: index_manager.go (new function near Bootstrap)
- Walk tree via walkTree, return map[relPath]*Node

### 6. Insert diff logic into Bootstrap()
- After successful load, before returning:
  1. collectFilesystemState -> collectSnapshotPaths
  2. Remove deleted: snapshot paths not in fsState
  3. Add new: fsState paths not in snapshot
  4. Update modified: file mtime differs from node ModTime
  5. Type mismatch: file became dir or vice versa
  6. If changes detected: mark dirty, update GeneratedAt

### 7. Add test TestBootstrapStaleSnapshot
- Create temp dir, bootstrap, add/delete/modify files, re-bootstrap
- Verify changes detected without LLM calls

### Pseudocode
diffAndApply(index, rootPath, ignored, cache):
  fsState = walkFilesystem(rootPath, ignored)
  snapPaths = walkSnapshotTree(index.Tree)
  changed = false
  for each snapPath not in fsState: remove -> changed
  for each fsState entry:
    if not in snapshot: upsert -> changed
    if file and mtime differs: upsert -> changed
    if type mismatch: upsert -> changed
  if changed: mark dirty, update GeneratedAt

### Risks
- Old snapshots without ModTime trigger one-time re-extraction (correct behavior)
- WalkDir performance acceptable (same as BuildTree minus symbol extraction)
- Race between diff and watch startup: watch catches subsequent changes

### Edge Cases
- Empty snapshot: falls through to full rebuild (existing)
- Root path mismatch: falls through to full rebuild (existing)
- No changes: returns immediately (same speed as today)
- Synonym cache preserved: keys by basename, not path
close_reason: Implemented: Bootstrap() now diffs filesystem against loaded snapshot on startup. Adds ModTime to Node, collectFilesystemState/collectSnapshotPaths helpers, diff logic in Bootstrap(). Test passes.

title: Phase 2: Extend Bench Engines — Token Counting + Hit@k
description:
## Summary

Add output size (token estimate) and Hit@1/Hit@3/Hit@5 scoring to every engine's EngineResult. Currently only contexting has rank — extend to all engines.

## Struct Changes (bench_engine.go)

```go
// EngineResult — extend with new fields
type EngineResult struct {
	EngineName string   `json:"engine_name"`
	Found      bool     `json:"found"`
	Rank       int      `json:"rank"`
	TotalHits  int      `json:"total_hits"`
	Paths      []string `json:"paths,omitempty"`
	TimeMs     int64    `json:"time_ms"`
	Error      string   `json:"error,omitempty"`
	// NEW:
	Chars  int   `json:"chars"`     // total chars across all returned paths
	Tokens int   `json:"tokens"`    // chars/4 heuristic
	HitAt1 bool  `json:"hit_at_1"`
	HitAt3 bool  `json:"hit_at_3"`
	HitAt5 bool  `json:"hit_at_5"`
}

// EngineSummary — extend with Hit@k rates, avg tokens
type EngineSummary struct {
	EngineName  string  `json:"engine_name"`
	Cases       int     `json:"cases"`
	Recall      float64 `json:"recall"`
	AvgResults  float64 `json:"avg_results"`
	AvgTimeMs   float64 `json:"avg_time_ms"`
	P50TimeMs   int64   `json:"p50_time_ms"`
	P95TimeMs   int64   `json:"p95_time_ms"`
	FailedCases int     `json:"failed_cases"`
	// NEW:
	HitAt1    float64 `json:"hit_at_1"`
	HitAt3    float64 `json:"hit_at_3"`
	HitAt5    float64 `json:"hit_at_5"`
	AvgTokens float64 `json:"avg_tokens"`
}
```

## Changes

### bench_engine.go
- Add `Chars`, `Tokens`, `HitAt1`, `HitAt3`, `HitAt5` to `EngineResult`
- Add `HitAt1`, `HitAt3`, `HitAt5`, `AvgTokens` to `EngineSummary`
- Add helper `computeHitAtK(paths []string, expectAny []string) (hit1, hit3, hit5 bool, firstRank int)`:
  - Returns 1-based rank of first expected match in paths, or -1
  - For contexting: paths already ranked. For find/grep/combined: paths sorted alphabetically
  - hit1 = firstRank == 1, hit3 = firstRank > 0 && <= 3, hit5 = firstRank > 0 && <= 5
- Add helper `countTokens(paths []string) int`:
  - Sum len(path) for all paths → chars. tokens = chars / 4
- In each engine's `Search()` method: after collecting paths, call computeHitAtK and countTokens, populate new fields
- Update `summarizeEngine()` (or equivalent aggregation function):
  - HitAt1 = count(hit1==true) / totalCases
  - HitAt3 = count(hit3==true) / totalCases
  - HitAt5 = count(hit5==true) / totalCases
  - AvgTokens = mean(tokens across all cases)

### bench_report.go
- Update table output to include Hit@1, Hit@3, Hit@5, Avg Tokens columns
- Update JSON output to include new summary fields

## Tests (bench_test.go)
- TestComputeHitAtK — expected file at rank 1, 3, 5, not found
- TestCountTokens — known path list → expected token count
- TestEngineResultTokenCounting — engine result includes correct token count
- TestSummaryHitAtK — summary correctly aggregates Hit@k rates
- Existing 7 tests still pass

## Dependencies
- Requires Phase 1 (contexting-hv4) — needs EvalCase.FindPattern/GrepPattern for fair baseline patterns

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] EngineResult has Chars, Tokens, HitAt1, HitAt3, HitAt5 fields
- [ ] EngineSummary has HitAt1, HitAt3, HitAt5, AvgTokens fields
- [ ] computeHitAtK helper works for ranked and unranked result lists
- [ ] countTokens helper uses chars/4 heuristic
- [ ] All 4 engines (contexting, find, grep, combined) populate new fields
- [ ] Summary aggregation includes Hit@k rates and avg tokens
- [ ] Report table and JSON output include new columns
- [ ] go test ./... passes
- [ ] Existing bench tests unchanged and passing
close_reason: Phase 2 complete. EngineResult + EngineSummary extended with Hit@k + token fields. computeHitAtK + countTokens helpers added. All 4 engines updated. Report includes new columns. 4 new tests pass.

title: Phase 5: Noise Ratio + Cold Start Timing Metrics
description:
## Summary

Add two extra credibility metrics to bench reports: noise ratio (% of results that are irrelevant) and cold start timing (index build cost context).

## Noise Ratio

What % of returned results are irrelevant (not in expect_any)?
- Contexting returns 10 ranked results → maybe 3 relevant. grep returns 50 lines → 3 relevant
- Shows signal-to-noise advantage, not just "did it find it"

### Changes (bench_engine.go)
- Add `NoiseRatio float64` to `EngineResult`:
  ```go
  NoiseRatio float64 `json:"noise_ratio"` // 1.0 - (relevantResults / totalResults)
  ```
- Compute: `noiseRatio = 1.0 - (matchedCount / totalResults)` where matchedCount = paths matching expect_any
- If totalResults == 0, noiseRatio = 0
- Add `AvgNoiseRatio float64` to `EngineSummary`

### Changes (bench_report.go)
- Add Noise column to per-category and overall tables
- Include in JSON output

## Cold Start Timing

Report index build time as context for search speed comparison.
- Contexting has index build cost (init) that find/grep don't
- Measure and report: "index build: 4.2s one-time, then 12ms/query vs grep 45ms/query"
- Honest about tradeoff — builds trust

### Changes (command_bench.go)
- At start of bench run, if using contexting engine, measure index load time:
  ```go
  start := time.Now()
  // load index
  indexLoadMs := time.Since(start).Milliseconds()
  ```
- Pass indexLoadMs to report function
- Print in report header: "Index load: Xms (one-time cost)"

### Changes (bench_report.go)
- Add index load time to report header
- Include in JSON output as `index_load_ms` field

## Tests (bench_test.go)
- TestNoiseRatioComputation — known results → expected noise ratio
- TestNoiseRatioEmptyResults — zero results → noise ratio 0
- TestNoiseRatioAllRelevant — all results relevant → noise ratio 0
- TestSummaryNoiseRatio — summary aggregates avg noise ratio correctly

## Dependencies
- Requires Phase 2 (contexting-7sl) — extends EngineResult/EngineSummary structs

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] EngineResult has NoiseRatio field
- [ ] EngineSummary has AvgNoiseRatio field
- [ ] Noise ratio computed as 1.0 - (relevant/total)
- [ ] Report tables include Noise column
- [ ] Index load time measured and displayed in report header
- [ ] JSON output includes noise_ratio and index_load_ms
- [ ] go test ./... passes
close_reason: Phase 5 complete. NoiseRatio on EngineResult, AvgNoiseRatio on EngineSummary. countRelevantPaths helper reuses normalizeEvalPath. Cold start timing (Index load: Xms). Noise column in all report modes.

title: Add contexting sync command for targeted synonym generation
notes:
## What

New  command. Scans the index, finds names with zero synonyms or fewer than configured, generates synonyms for just those names.

## Behavior

1. Load existing context.json
2. Collect all names from tree via CollectNamesForLLM
3. For each name, check synonym cache:
   - Not in cache → needs synonyms
   - In cache but len(synonyms) < cfg.Common.SynonymsPerName (default 4) → needs more
4. Generate synonyms only for names that need them
5. Update tree nodes with new synonyms
6. Update synonym cache
7. Flush updated context.json

## Command



Flags:
- Standard CommonFlags (model, api-key, endpoint, etc.)
- Inherits config from context.toml

## Output



If no names need synonyms:


## Implementation

- New file: command_sync.go
- Register in commands.go (add alongside init, watch, search)
- Reuse: LoadContextIndex, CollectNamesForLLM, LoadSynonymCache, GenerateSynonymsForNamesWithContext, FlushIfDirty
- Should work even if watch is running (atomic file writes)
- Should work standalone (no watch needed)

## Files

- command_sync.go (new)
- commands.go (register new command)

## Key Functions to Reuse

- LoadContextIndex() — load snapshot
- CollectNamesForLLM() — get all names from tree
- LoadSynonymCache() — load cache
- GenerateSynonymsForNamesWithContext() — LLM calls
- FlushIfDirty() — save updated index
- resolveLLMConfig() — resolve API key, endpoint, etc.
close_reason: Implemented: command_sync.go created, registered in commands.go. Loads index, identifies names missing/short on synonyms, generates only those, updates tree and cache.

description:

title: Phase 1: Case Format v2 + Categories
description:
## Summary

Upgrade eval/bench case file format to v2 with category grouping and optional baseline pattern fields. Backward compatible with v1 (bare JSON array).

## v2 JSON Format

```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "categories": {
    "path-intent": {
      "description": "Find a file by describing its path/location purpose",
      "cases": [
        {
          "query": "auth middleware",
          "expect_any": ["internal/middleware/auth.go"],
          "description": "Locate the authentication middleware file",
          "find_pattern": "auth",
          "grep_pattern": "auth"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

## Go Structs

```go
type CaseFile struct {
	Version    int                    `json:"version"`
	Categories map[string]CaseCategory `json:"categories"`
}

type CaseCategory struct {
	Description string     `json:"description"`
	Cases       []EvalCase `json:"cases"`
}

// Extend existing EvalCase in-place with omitempty fields:
type EvalCase struct {
	Query       string   `json:"query"`
	ExpectAny   []string `json:"expect_any"`
	Description string   `json:"description,omitempty"`  // NEW
	FindPattern string   `json:"find_pattern,omitempty"` // NEW
	GrepPattern string   `json:"grep_pattern,omitempty"` // NEW
	Category    string   `json:"category,omitempty"`     // NEW — set when loaded from v2
}
```

## Changes

### eval.go
- Extend `EvalCase` struct with `Description`, `FindPattern`, `GrepPattern`, `Category` (all omitempty)
- Add `CaseFile` and `CaseCategory` types
- Add `LoadCasesAuto(path string) ([]EvalCase, error)`:
  - Peek first non-whitespace byte: `[` → v1 (unmarshal []EvalCase), `{` → v2 (unmarshal CaseFile)
  - For v2: assert version==2, sort category keys alphabetically, set Category on each case, flatten
- Keep existing `LoadEvalCases` unchanged (tests reference it)

### command_eval.go
- Replace `LoadEvalCases(casesPath)` with `LoadCasesAuto(casesPath)`

### command_bench.go
- Replace `LoadEvalCases(casesPath)` with `LoadCasesAuto(casesPath)`

## Categories
- path-intent, symbol-lookup, concept-synonym, exact-file, narrow-scope, vague-intent

## Tests (eval_test.go or cases_v2_test.go)
- TestLoadCasesV1Array — v1 array still loads, new fields default to zero
- TestLoadCasesV2Object — v2 object loads, categories flatten, Category field set, deterministic order
- TestLoadCasesV2MissingVersion — error on object without version: 2
- TestLoadCasesV2EmptyCategories — returns empty slice, no error
- TestLoadCasesAutoDetectsV1 — bare array path
- TestLoadCasesAutoDetectsV2 — object path
- TestEvalCaseV1UnmarshalIgnoresNewFields — v1 JSON with only query/expect_any still works

## Risks
- Category ordering: Go maps unordered → sort keys alphabetically for deterministic case order
- EvalCase used by both eval and bench → adding omitempty fields is safe, verify no strict struct comparison
- Backward compat: v1 files must still work, handle leading whitespace/BOM in peek

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] EvalCase extended with 4 new omitempty fields
- [ ] CaseFile and CaseCategory types defined
- [ ] LoadCasesAuto handles both v1 (array) and v2 (object) formats
- [ ] v1 case files still load without modification
- [ ] v2 case files load with categories flattened and Category field set
- [ ] Category keys sorted alphabetically for deterministic order
- [ ] command_eval.go and command_bench.go use LoadCasesAuto
- [ ] go test ./... passes with all existing tests unchanged
- [ ] New tests cover v1 compat, v2 loading, auto-detection, edge cases
close_reason: Phase 1 complete. EvalCase extended, CaseFile/CaseCategory types added, LoadCasesAuto handles v1+v2, call sites updated, 7 tests pass.

title: Phase 4: Seed 30-50 Real Benchmark Cases
description:
## Summary

Create a case file with 30-50 realistic test cases across all 6 categories using v2 format. Cases should reflect real developer queries. Include find_pattern/grep_pattern for fair baselines.

## Categories (target 5-8 cases each)

| Category | Example query | Tests |
|----------|---------------|-------|
| path-intent | "auth middleware" | Fuzzy path matching |
| symbol-lookup | "handleLogin function" | Symbol extraction |
| concept-synonym | "payment processing" | LLM synonym expansion |
| exact-file | "config.toml" | Baseline — all tools should nail |
| narrow-scope | "test for user model" | Filtering noise |
| vague-intent | "where is rate limiting" | Conceptual search |

## Case File Location
- `docs/bench_cases.json` — versioned, shareable, not project-specific
- Can also copy to `.ctx/ctx_cases.json` for local use

## Case Structure (v2 format)
Each case needs:
- `query` — what a developer would type
- `expect_any` — array of expected file paths (relative to project root)
- `description` — why this case is interesting
- `find_pattern` — hand-tuned pattern for find engine (optional but recommended)
- `grep_pattern` — hand-tuned pattern for grep engine (optional but recommended)

## Approach
1. Scan the contexting codebase itself for realistic cases:
   - Functions in symbols.go, search.go, indexer.go, etc.
   - Files like command_bench.go, bench_engine.go, etc.
   - Config files, test files, docs
2. Write cases that test different search modalities:
   - Exact file name matches (exact-file)
   - Path-based fuzzy matching (path-intent)
   - Symbol/function lookups (symbol-lookup)
   - Conceptual/synonym matches (concept-synonym)
   - Scoped queries with noise (narrow-scope)
   - Vague conceptual queries (vague-intent)
3. For each case, write fair find_pattern and grep_pattern
4. Validate: run `contexting bench --cases docs/bench_cases.json` and verify results

## Dependencies
- Requires Phase 1 (contexting-hv4) — needs v2 case format

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 30-50 cases total across 6 categories
- [ ] Each case has query, expect_any, description
- [ ] Most cases have find_pattern and grep_pattern
- [ ] Cases cover all 6 categories with 5-8 each
- [ ] File uses v2 format with version: 2
- [ ] Cases are realistic — reflect actual developer queries
- [ ] `contexting bench --cases docs/bench_cases.json` runs successfully
close_reason: Phase 4 complete. 45 cases across 6 categories in docs/bench_cases.json. All paths verified real. Bench runs successfully.

title: Add contexting bench command — compare search quality vs find/grep
description:
## Summary

Add a new `contexting bench` subcommand that runs the same search queries through multiple search engines (contexting, find, grep) and produces a comparison report. This lets us quantify how contexting\s semantic search holds up against traditional filesystem search tools.

## Why

The existing `contexting eval` command already tests contexting against predefined expected paths (Hit@1/3/5, MRR). But it does not compare against find or grep. We need to know:

- Does contexting find files that find/grep miss?
- Is it faster or slower?
- How noisy are the results (precision/recall trade-off)?
- How does ranking quality differ?

## Design Decisions

### Engine: contexting
- **Imports search logic directly** — calls `SearchHintsWithOptions()` from the same `package main`. No exec overhead.
- Loads the same `.ctx/ctx_index.json` index.
- Full ranking, all matching features (symbols, synonyms, path, basename).

### Engine: find
- **Pure filename matching** via `filepath.WalkDir`.
- Query tokens matched against basename and path segments (same tokenization as contexting).
- No ranking — results are unordered (or alphabetically sorted).
- Simulates `find . -iname "*token*"` but in-process and cross-platform.

### Engine: grep
- **Content matching** — reads files (up to a size limit) and checks if query tokens appear in contents.
- Respects same ignore patterns as contexting (no need to search vendored deps).
- No ranking — results are unordered.
- Simulates `grep -ril "keyword"` but in-process, cross-platform, and with ignore rules.

### Engine: combined
- Union of find + grep results.
- Deduplicated by path.

## What We Measure

Per query, per engine:

| Metric | What it means |
|--------|---------------|
| `found` | Was the expected file in the results? (boolean) |
| `rank` | Position of first expected match (contexting only, N/A for find/grep) |
| `total_results` | How many paths returned (noise indicator) |
| `time_ms` | Wall time in milliseconds |
| `precision` | % of results that were relevant (subjective — best effort from test cases) |

Aggregate across all cases:

| Metric | What it means |
|--------|---------------|
| `recall` | % of cases where expected file was found |
| `hit_at_k` | % found in top K (contexting only) |
| `avg_results` | Mean result count per query |
| `mean_time` | Mean execution time |
| `p50/p95_time` | Latency distribution |

## Files to Create

### `command_bench.go` (new)
- Cobra command registration: `contexting bench`
- Flags: `--cases`, `--index`, `--limit`, `--min-score`, `--json`, `--engines`
- Config integration: reads `[bench]` section from `.ctx/ctx_config.toml`
- Runner: loads cases, iterates, dispatches to engines, collects results
- Calls report formatting

### `bench_engine.go` (new)
- `SearchEngine` interface with `Name()`, `Search()` methods
- `ContextingEngine` — wraps `SearchHintsWithOptions()`, loads index
- `FindEngine` — filepath.WalkDir + basename/segment matching
- `GrepEngine` — filepath.WalkDir + content reading + keyword matching
- `CombinedEngine` — union of Find + Grep

### `bench_report.go` (new)
- `printBenchSummary()` — terminal table output
- `resultsToBenchJSON()` — JSON output for scripting

## Files to Modify

### `commands.go`
- Add `rootCmd.AddCommand(newBenchCommand())` line
- Add `"bench"` to `agentUnsafeCommands`? No — bench is read-only, no state change. Skip.

### `config.go`
- Add `BenchConfig` struct with fields: `CasesPath`, `IndexPath`, `Limit`, `MinScore`, `Engines`, `Json`
- Add `Bench BenchConfig` field to `ContextingConfig`

### `config_template.go`
- Add `[bench]` section to starter config template with defaults

## Test Cases Format

Reuses the same JSON format as `contexting eval`:

```json
[
  {"query": "batch audio processing", "expect_any": ["badwords-editor-solid/cli_batch.go"]},
  {"query": "transcribe handler", "expect_any": ["lyricut-back-front/back/lyricut-back/internal/handlers/transcribe_handler.go"]},
  {"query": "cli installation", "expect_any": ["badwords-editor-solid/cli_install.go"]},
  {"query": "profanity detector", "expect_any": ["lyricut-cli/detect.go"]},
  {"query": "release workflow", "expect_any": [".github/workflows/release.yml"]}
]
```

These initial cases are specific to the lyricut-editor monorepo but the tool works on any project — just provide appropriate test cases.

## Output Example

```
$ contexting bench --cases .ctx/ctx_cases.json
```

title: feat: add contexting bench command for cross-engine search comparison
description:
## Summary

Add a `contexting bench` command that runs the same set of eval queries through multiple search engines (contexting, find, grep) and compares their performance — recall, result count, and wall time — in a table or JSON report.

This lets developers benchmark contexting against standard filesystem tools to validate improvement claims.

## Why

The existing `contexting eval` measures how well contexting finds expected files (Hit@1/3/5, MRR). But it doesn't answer: "how much better is this than just using find or grep?" This command answers that directly — same queries, same expected paths, cross-engine comparison.

## Design

### Engines compared

- **contexting** — Shells out to `contexting search-hints "query" --json` (ranked)
- **find** — `find . -iname "*token*"` per token, union of results (unranked, filename-only)
- **grep** — `grep -ril "token"` per token across source extensions, union (unranked, content-based)
- **combined** — Union of find + grep results (best-effort baseline)

### Metrics per query

- **Found?** — Did the engine return any path matching `expect_any`?
- **Rank** (contexting only) — Position of first expected hit
- **Result count** — Total paths returned (signal-to-noise proxy)
- **Wall time** — Real time taken (ms) via subprocess timing

### Summary (over all cases)

Example output:
```
                recall    avg_results   avg_time
contexting      92%       2.4            12ms
find            42%       38.1           195ms
grep            75%       14.2           780ms
combined        83%       46.3           810ms
```

### Output modes

- **Table** (default) — Human-readable aligned columns
- **--json** — Full structured output for scripting

### Reuses existing format

Uses the same `EvalCase` JSON format as `contexting eval`:
```
[
  {"query": "auth middleware", "expect_any": ["internal/auth/middleware.go"]}
]
```
So test cases are portable between eval and bench.

## Files to create

```
bench/
├── main.go        # Entry: flags, dispatch, command registration
├── runners.go     # Engine interface + implementations (contexting, find, grep, combined)
├── report.go      # Table formatting + JSON output
└── bench_test.go  # Unit tests
```

## Implementation approach

1. Add `newBenchCommand()` cobra command to `commands.go`
2. Engines run as goroutines per case
3. contexting engine: `exec.Command("contexting", "search-hints", query, "--json", "--limit", "10")` with --root flag
4. find engine: split query into tokens, run find per token, union + dedupe
5. grep engine: split query into tokens, grep -ril per token across source extensions, union + dedupe
6. combined engine: union of find + grep results
7. Scoring: normalize paths and compare against expect_any (same as eval's firstMatchRank)
8. Timing: time.Now() before/after each engine call

## Registration

Add `newBenchCommand()` to `commands.go` alongside the existing 9 subcommands.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `contexting bench --cases cases.json` prints comparison table
- [ ] `contexting bench --cases cases.json --json` outputs full structured JSON
- [ ] Each engine reports found/not-found, result count, and wall time per case
- [ ] Summary row aggregates recall, avg results, avg time
- [ ] Works with existing ctx_index.json
- [ ] Handle edge cases: empty query, no cases file, binary not in PATH (graceful error)
- [ ] `go test ./bench/...` passes
